impacts.description: traffic jams and road closures in the capital, including Lope de Vega Avenue, Julio Cortázar Avenue, and other streets

evidence.quote: There have also been some traffic jams and road closures in the capital, such as on Lope de Vega Avenue, heading towards the city center, near Julio Cortázar Avenue due to a road subsidence.

impacts.description: flight delays of approximately 15 minutes for flights scheduled during the early morning hours at Malaga Airport

evidence.quote: At Malaga Airport, a severe thunderstorm forced air traffic control to implement traffic management measures to ensure safety, causing delays of approximately 15 minutes for flights scheduled during the early morning hours.

impacts.description: heavy rainfall recorded 47.3 liters per square meter in the Guadalhorce River, 43.4 liters in the city of Málaga, 42.9 liters in Pujerra, 41.6 liters in Sierra de Mijas, 31.3 liters in Torre del Mar, 31.2 liters in Ronda, and various reservoirs

evidence.quote: In the last 12 hours, 47.3 liters per square meter have been recorded in the Guadalhorce River; 43.4 liters in the city of Málaga (Paseo de la Farola); 42.9 liters in the town of Pujerra; 41.6 liters in the Sierra de Mijas; 31.3 liters in Torre del Mar, part of Vélez-Málaga; and 31.2 liters in Ronda. Rainfall has also been recorded in some reservoirs, such as Guadalteba, with 42 liters per square meter; Conde del Guadalhorce, with 40.5 liters; Limonero, with 34.8 liters; La Viñuela, with 21.2 liters; and La Concepción, with 16.9 liters per square meter.

impacts.description: heavy rainfall recorded 40 liters in various locations, including the capital city and the Sierra de Mijas mountain range

evidence.quote: The heavy rains that fell early Tuesday morning in the province of Málaga have left more than 40 liters in various locations, including the capital city and the Sierra de Mijas mountain range.

impacts.description: heavy rainfall recorded 30 liters per square meter in one hour and 80 liters accumulated in 12 hours in the orange alert area

evidence.quote: The State Meteorological Agency (Aemet) maintains the orange alert active until midday in the Malaga regions of Costa del Sol and Guadalhorce due to storms and rainfall that can reach 30 liters per square meter in one hour and 80 liters accumulated in 12 hours.

impacts.description: private Novaschool Sunland International school in Cártama had to cancel classes due to a considerable flood that made access impossible

evidence.quote: Some educational centers, such as the private Novaschool Sunland International school located in the municipality of Cártama, have had to cancel their classes this Tuesday due to the heavy rainfall, which has caused a considerable flood in the vicinity of the center that has made access to it impossible.
